newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom eases after "no surprises" profit.
newsitem.headline: Telecom eases after "no surprises" profit.

text.p: Shares in Telecom Corp of New Zealand eased slightly on Wednesday but on very light volume, reflecting a "no surprises" annual result.
Telecom earlier reported a slump in year net profit to NZ$581.4 million from $716.8 million.
By 12.40 p.m. (0040 GMT) the share price was down just three cents to NZ$6.65, having earlier sunk to $6.60. But turnover of just over 246,000 shares was very light.
Murray Rutherford, broker at SBC Warburg, said normalised earnings of NZ$770.5 million were very close to forecasts.

Rutherford noted Telecom had taken some big, one-off "hits". "The company has taken some big one-off provisions this year, notably from (Australian unit) Pacific Star, and also for its millenium problems, but they would be expected to be non-recurring items," he said.
